answer_1.quote: We formalize SLJA as four interrelated tasks (See Figure ): (1) article retrieval (AR) selects relevant articles from article database as a major premise; (2) criminal element generation (CEG) generates the criminal elements of a fact as a minor premise; (3) article interpretation generation (AIG) produces the applicable articles and corresponding rationale according to major and minor premises; (4) legal judgment prediction (LJP) generates the judgments results according to the applicable articles.
answer_1.outputs: Generated criminal elements, article interpretations, charges, and terms of penalty.

answer_2.quote: For CEG task, we extract criminal elements from the generated results by regular expressions and evaluate these elements with specific metrics, respectively. Precision (P), Recall (R), and F1 score are used to evaluate the performance of subjective element prediction... Match score evaluates the exact matches between generated items and human-corrected ones. ROUGE score evaluates the word overlap between generated subject, objective elements, and object and manually corrected ones.

answer_4.quote: We hire 22 workers with a legal background to work on the correction process.
answer_4.guideline: The guideline introduces the definition of each task, the detailed system operations, and an example of data correction.
